Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

news noun

information about recent events

also tidings, I just got news that, no news, the news, good news, bad news

classical

Plaut. Stich. 2.2.67: nūntium exoptābilem nūntiāre (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 350

nūntius, nūntiī m.

noun, second declension

news, a message, tidings (especially news brought by someone)

Other words

  • novī (quid novī, nihil novī) — news: “something new”, the genitive with a neuter pronoun

    genitive of novum after quid, aliquid, nihil · classical · Traupman 350, 104

    Latin asks for “anything of new”: quid novī?, any news?; nihil novī, no news (see any news?).

Examples

  • Modo mihi nūntiātum est (+ acc. and inf.)

    I just got news that …Traupman 350

  • Sī nihil novī habēs dē (+ abl.) …

    If you have no news about …Traupman 350

See also any news?, message, newspaper.

SourcesLewis & Short: nuntius · Lewis & Short: novus

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 350.
